criterion_notes.c1: Examines household access to safe, climate-resilient on-site sanitation infrastructure (purchase/order of Easy Latrine or elevated Sky Latrine) among rural households without a toilet in Kampong Chhnang province, Cambodia.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies Criterion 2 under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain reading, it examines an administrative and institutional subsidy-targeting and eligibility-assessment mechanism incorporating Cambodia's government IDPoor social-protection poverty classification, commune-level Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) designations from the National Council for Sustainable Development, and local village authority involvement. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, although implemented by an NGO (iDE) within market-based sanitation delivery rather than as a statutory mandate, the study directly designs, tests, and disaggregates a formal eligibility-screening and targeted-pricing rule (comparing government IDPoor eligibility against a three-threshold Poverty Probability Index [PPI] proxy means test calibrated to climate vulnerability, alongside frontline screener misinterpretation of exclusion rules, village-leader targeting bias, threshold gaming/manipulation checks, and verification burden), squarely fitting 'eligibility screening' and targeted cost-recovery/subsidy rules governing service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Mixed-methods empirical study combining a 30-village cluster randomized controlled trial (2,821 unique household sales presentations analyzed via village-level OLS and clustered household-level logistic regressions), 13 qualitative key-stakeholder interviews (latrine business owners, local government representatives, and sales agents) analyzed in ATLAS.ti, and programmatic cost/scalability analysis.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports household-level latrine purchase (binary order/sales conversion for climate-resilient Easy Latrine or Sky Latrine) and village-level latrine sales closing rates across eligible and ineligible groups, directly measuring affordability-mediated sanitation acquisition and exclusion (noting as a limitation that orders rather than completed installations were tracked).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies population and units of analysis (rural households without an existing toilet across 30 villages in Kampong Chhnang province, analyzed at both household [n = 2,821 presentations] and village [n = 30 clusters] levels, plus n = 13 qualitative stakeholder interviews), exposure (village-level randomized offer of a 50% targeted latrine price subsidy governed by IDPoor and climate-adjusted PPI eligibility screening thresholds vs. full retail price, and comparison across IDPoor vs. PPI eligibility pathways), outcome (latrine purchase/order conversion), and study design (mixed-methods cluster RCT).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: In treatment areas, eligible households were offered the option to purchase a latrine with a subsidy, while households in control areas could only purchase at retail price.
This research sought to build upon a previously used subsidy mechanism that relied upon the existing IDPoor mechanism, a Cambodian government poverty classiﬁcation, for targeting.

Determining an individual household’s eligibility to receive a subsidy required comparing their overall PPI score to the threshold that aligned with their household and community-level climate vulnerability.
Many sales agents believed qualiﬁcation was predicated on one factor (namely, the number of household members or ownership of a cell phone) and that this was unfairly excluding certain households.
Field implementation lasted 7.5 months (20 January 2022–31 August 2022) and included 2,821 sales presentations across 30 villages in Kampong Chhnang province.
In treatment areas, the sales closing rate among households who were offered a subsidy was 38%, compared to 6% among ineligible households

raw_response.exposure: Targeted 50% latrine price subsidy governed by a two-layer eligibility screening rule combining Cambodia's government IDPoor poverty classification, commune-level Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) scores, household climate-shock history, and three Poverty Probability Index (PPI) cutoff thresholds (assigned at the village cluster level vs. retail-price-only control villages, and compared across IDPoor vs. PPI eligibility pathways)
raw_response.outcome: Household latrine purchase (order/sales conversion for concrete-lined Easy Latrine or elevated Sky Latrine) and village-level latrine sales closing rate, alongside eligibility/exclusion rates and market distortion indicators
raw_response.population_and_sample: Rural households without a toilet in Kampong Chhnang province (Tonle Sap Lake region), Cambodia: 2,821 unique household sales presentations across 30 villages (15 treatment, 15 control; analyzed at household and village cluster levels), plus 13 in-depth qualitative interviews with latrine business owners, local government representatives, and sales agents
raw_response.rationale: This English-language mixed-methods cluster RCT in rural Cambodia meets all inclusion criteria (c1–c6). It examines household access to climate-resilient on-site sanitation (c1) and reports empirical quantitative and qualitative evidence on household latrine purchase/order rates and village sales closing rates (c3, c4, c5). On Criterion 2, both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading are satisfied: rather than evaluating generic project delivery alone, the study designs, tests, and disaggregates a formal eligibility-screening and targeted-subsidy pricing rule that integrates Cambodia's official IDPoor social-protection poverty registry and National Council for Sustainable Development commune CVI classifications with climate-adjusted PPI proxy-means-test cutoff thresholds, and explicitly analyzes differential uptake across IDPoor vs. PPI screening rules, village-authority targeting, frontline agent misinterpretation of eligibility rules, threshold manipulation checks, and verification burden.
raw_response.study_design: Mixed-methods cluster randomized controlled trial (30 villages) with qualitative key-informant interviews and programmatic cost analysis
